short: The last Catholic monarch of England, Scotland, and Ireland, whose deposition during the Glorious Revolution ended absolute monarchy.
full:
James II of England and VII of Scotland ascended to the throne in 1685 following the death of his brother, Charles II. A devout Catholic in a fiercely Protestant nation, his short reign was marked by growing religious and political tension. James appointed Catholics to key military and political positions, suspended penal laws against religious minorities, and alienated the Anglican establishment. The birth of a Catholic heir in June 1688 precipitated a crisis, as it threatened to establish a permanent Catholic dynasty.

In November 1688, a coalition of Protestant nobles invited William of Orange, James's son-in-law, to invade England. As his support collapsed and his army defected, James fled to France in December. Parliament subsequently declared that he had abdicated. The ensuing Glorious Revolution established a constitutional monarchy with the 1689 Bill of Rights, explicitly barring Catholics from the British succession and ending the Stuart doctrine of divine right. James spent the rest of his life in exile, launching one major unsuccessful attempt to regain his thrones via Ireland, which culminated in his defeat at the Battle of the Boyne in 1690.
